title: ACME - POC scoping for inference workload - Redwood kickoff
summary: Kickoff for a 6-week POC to validate inference latency, throughput and cost for Acme Logistics use case (shipment ETA prediction + chat assistant). Key milestones: kickoff, VPC/access setup, benchmark runs, midpoint review, exec readout. Success criteria: latency and cost targets + quality threshold. Next steps and action items captured.
next_steps: Redwood to share Dedicated performance spreadsheet, POC plan, and security docs (SOC2, network checklist)
Acme to provide representative sample dataset and production traffic profile (token distribution)
Acme infra to provision VPC peering and service account for Redwood test cluster
Schedule midpoint review (tentative 2025-03-24) and exec readout (tentative 2025-04-11)
action_items: Jamie Chen - Send POC runbook, benchmark template, and pricing assumptions (due: 2025-03-06)
Liam Patel - Prepare dedicated perf spreadsheet and initial perf run scripts (due: 2025-03-07)
Tom Nguyen - Share sample dataset and QPS/token distribution CSV (due: 2025-03-05)
Acme Infra - Provision VPC peering and IAM service account for Redwood (due: 2025-03-10)
Maria Gonzalez - Confirm exec stakeholders and availability for readout (due: 2025-03-12)
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-03-04
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Patel (Redwood SE), Maria Gonzalez (Acme PM), Tom Nguyen (Acme Eng), Rajesh Kumar (Acme Dir, AI)

Summary: Kickoff for ACME POC focusing on inference workload sizing, benchmarks, and timeline. Discussed success criteria (latency, cost, quality), access/security (VPC, KMS), and milestones: kickoff, access/setup, benchmark runs, mid-point review, exec readout.

Topics: POC timeline & milestones; success criteria; workload sizing; benchmark plan; access & security requirements.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jamie: Hey everybody thanks for joining, this is Jamie from Redwood, i'm the AE on the deal. we'll do a quick intros and then free to jump into the poc plan.
[00:12] Maria: hi, Maria here, PM for the logistics chat and ETA prediction feature. Tom's on the infra side and Rajesh is our AI lead. thanks for running this.
[00:20] Tom: hey all, morning.
[00:22] Rajesh: afternoon from me, excited to get moving.
[00:25] Liam: cool, i'm Liam, solutions engineer at Redwood, i'll own the bench runs and perf config. quick note, sometimes our notes autotranscribe Redwood as red wood or redWood dediate, so ignore that if it shows up.
[00:34] Jamie: quick agenda: align success criteria, agree sizing and benchmarks, confirm access & security, and lock the timeline + milestones. any additions?
[00:40] Maria: sounds good. also want clarity on what counts as pass/fail for execs — latency vs quality tradeoffs.
[00:47] Jamie: perfect, we'll cover that. to start, can you walk us through expected workload? QPS, typical tokens per request?
[00:54] Tom: sure, for chat assistant average request ~120 tokens, peak concurrency around 50 concurrent sessions, steady qps around 40 req/s with short bursts to 150 qps during peak. For the ETA prediction batch job it's more throughput oriented, roughly 2k requests/hour but each request is small (~30 tokens) but we may run re-ranking flows that are heavier.
[01:15] Liam: that's helpful. for sizing we'll plan for a baseline bench with 50 concurrent users and an emulated peak burst test to 150 qps. we'll also run token-heavy rerank flows as a separate benchmark.
[01:25] Rajesh: target p50 latency for chat should be <200ms and p95 < 400ms, otherwise execs will question it. on cost we want to see per-1M token cost under a reasonable threshold, ballpark $60 - $100 / 1M tokens depending on model. quality target: top-1 accuracy / rerank score above 0.85 on our eval prompts and hallucination <2%.
[01:45] Maria: yes those are the right levers. can Redwood run with our private deployment? we need VPC and KMS integration for keys.
[01:52] Jamie: absolutely, we support Redwood Private (private control plane + VPC peering) and Dedicated pools. for the poc we can do a dedicated test pool in your VPC or a secure test env with peering — whichever you prefer. we'll need a service account and peering details.
[02:10] Tom: we'll prefer peering into our dev VPC first. security team will ask for SOC2 + network diagram and what ports are required.
[02:18] Liam: noted. we'll share SOC2 report and an infra checklist. ports are fairly standard TLS endpoints and SSH to the bastion for setup; we'll send a one-page network checklist.
[02:29] Jamie: ok timeline proposal: 6-week POC. week 0 kickoff (today), week 1 access & env setup, week 2-3 benchmark runs and iteration, mid-point review at end of week 3, final validation and exec readout week 6. does that align with your expectations?
[02:46] Maria: that fits. can we tighten the mid-point earlier? we prefer a 2-week check to make sure we're not blocked.
[02:52] Liam: we can do a light mid-check at day 10 and a full mid-point at day 21. so: quick health check ~2025-03-14, full midpoint 2025-03-24.
[03:05] Rajesh: good. what does the bench plan look like? synthetic replay vs production traffic replay?
[03:12] Liam: plan is two-phase: 1) small-scale functional bench with synthetic load and your sample dataset to validate correctness and integration; 2) full-scale perf run with production traffic replay (we ask for token distribution CSV and a short replay window). we'll measure p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, and cost per 100k tokens as a proxy.
[03:33] Tom: we'll share replay traces and token histograms. note some of our real traffic has long tail prompts up to 800 tokens for debugging sessions.
[03:40] Liam: ok we'll include a long-tail test. for model choice: will you want to test multiple variants (quantized vs fp16) and compare? that impacts perf/cost tradeoffs.
[03:49] Maria: yes please, we want a recommended profile that balances cost and latency. if quantized model meets quality thresholds we'll favor it.
[03:56] Jamie: success criteria recap — pass if: latency targets met (p50 <200ms, p95 <400ms), rerank/quality threshold >0.85, and cost within agreed band. if not met, we document failure modes and recommendations (different model, more GPUs, batching/caching tuning).
[04:14] Rajesh: any SLA in POC? we need clear uptime for demo runs.
[04:19] Jamie: for POC we run best-effort but will provide scheduled windows and support from our SEs. if you later move to Dedicated we provide SLA per contract.
[04:28] Tom: about data retention — will logs persist in Redwood? we prefer no persistence beyond audit windows.
[04:34] Liam: we'll respect your retention policy; default is short-term logs for debugging, we can disable retention and only store minimal audit logs. we'll include KMS encryption options and key rollover notes.
[04:47] Maria: great. on roles: Jamie will drive coordination, Liam will run perf and bench, Tom will do infra, i'll coordinate product and exec calendar.
[04:57] Jamie: perfect. let's enumerate milestones and dates: kickoff 2025-03-04, access & env setup complete by 2025-03-10, initial bench runs by 2025-03-14 (light health check), full perf window and iteration 2025-03-17 to 2025-03-21, full midpoint review 2025-03-24, final validation and exec readout 2025-04-11. does that look ok?
[05:20] Maria: yes except maybe move exec readout to week of 4/07? we'll confirm.
[05:25] Jamie: ok we'll tentatively keep 4/11 and await Maria's confirm.
[05:30] Rajesh: what artifacts will Redwood provide after POC?
[05:33] Liam: we'll give a perf report (latency/throughput/cost), recommended model & quantization config, infra config docs, and an exec summary slide deck.
[05:43] Tom: will you provide the perf scripts so we can reproduce?
[05:46] Liam: yes, we'll hand over the benchmarking harness, load scripts, and the exact request traces used (redacted).
[05:53] Maria: security docs?
[05:55] Jamie: we'll send SOC2, ISO snippets, network checklist, and our data processing addendum. also will include instructions for KMS integration.
[06:05] Maria: ok great. any blockers we foresee?
[06:08] Tom: the VPC peering approval process can be slow — may need security review; we'll push it.
[06:13] Jamie: to mitigate we'll run an interim test using a secure tunnel if peering is delayed. that will let us start benching earlier.
[06:20] Rajesh: perfect. one more thing: can you run a small accuracy sweep on our eval set during week 2?
[06:25] Liam: yes, we'll do the eval sweep and share the numbers alongside perf.
[06:30] Maria: great — I think that's all from our side.
[06:33] Jamie: recap of action items: I'll send runbook and pricing, Liam provides perf sheet and scripts, Tom shares dataset and sets up infra, Maria will confirm exec invite list and availability. We'll aim for day-10 health check and full midpoint at day-21.
[06:48] Maria: thanks everyone. we'll expect the runbook by friday.
[06:51] Jamie: thanks, we'll follow up in email and create the calendar invites for the milestones.
[06:55] Liam: thanks, bye.
[06:57] Tom: bye.
[06:58] Rajesh: thanks all, bye.

End of transcript.
